description: Hatsu's two harness hooks. `Stop` rings the bell — an OS notification and a sound — when a gate stop is waiting, reading the marker the jutaisho skill drops at .nen/last-stop.json; `PreToolUse` on Bash refuses a `git commit` or a `git push` while the working copy sits on the workflow base branch. NEITHER IS A NEN-OWNED STEP. They are Claude Code hooks, executed by the harness around a session rather than by a skill inside one, and they exist because a notification and a reflex refusal are the two things a skill cannot do: a skill only runs when the model calls it, and by the time the model has stopped talking or has already typed the push, it is too late. Every deterministic step the skills themselves take stays a nen verb. Both scripts are POSIX sh, use no jq, yq or python (README, 'On the installed plugin path'), and fail open — a hook that cannot read what it needs stays out of the way rather than blocking a session on its own uncertainty. The guard is the deliberate exception, and it PARSES the command rather than matching a substring: a `sh -c '<script>'` wrapper is unwrapped, quoted spans are masked, the line is split into segments, and a segment counts only when its first token is `git` and the token after git's own global options (`-C`, `-c`, `--no-pager`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `--namespace`, in both the separate-argument and `--key=value` forms) is `commit` or `push` — so `echo 'git commit'` and `git commit-tree` pass while `git -C <dir> commit` and `git --git-dir=<dir>/.git commit` are judged in <dir>. It fails CLOSED on the four forms where the branch it can see is not the branch the write would land on: a line that both changes branch (switch, checkout, branch -f) and writes; a repository-selecting path it cannot recover; a git segment carrying a write token whose subcommand it cannot establish; and a shell wrapper whose payload it cannot read on a line that carries a write token.
